name: Godrej Agrovet Ltd
_note: Fact base to 30-Sep-2026 (Q1FY27 basis). Rs crore unless stated. Every figure carries a source key (see sources) and the source's publication date.

imd.what: IMD salient features of the 2026 south-west monsoon

duty.what: Business Today: edible-oil customs duty cut

profile: Diversified agri-business of the Godrej Industries group (incorporated 25-Nov-1991; listed Oct-2017 at ₹460). Six reported segments: Animal Nutrition (compound feed for cattle, poultry, fish and shrimp; India's largest organised cattle-feed maker), Vegetable Oil (India's largest crude palm oil producer from ~80,000 ha of farmer-owned plantations in AP, Telangana and other states), Crop Care (standalone branded agrochemicals plus 67.03%-owned listed Astec LifeSciences), Dairy (Creamline Dairy, 'Godrej Jersey', South India, 99.78% owned), Poultry & processed foods (Godrej Foods: Real Good Chicken, Yummiez; 100% owned since Aug-2024) and Others. 50% JV ACI Godrej Agrovet (Bangladesh feed). Holding company: Godrej Industries Ltd (65.05%).

q1fy27.nonRecurring: Employee separation provision ₹4 cr; deferred-tax remeasurement ₹5 cr credit

q1fy27.point: FY27 PBT: 'we'll be able to target a double-digit growth still' (May guidance was mid-teens); final view after Q2.

June rainfall ~40% deficit hit cotton-herbicide volumes; July better; recovery view only by end-September; FY27 standalone EBIT margin ~26-27%; Ashitaka + Takai ~18-20% of Q1 sales; Ghassnash soybean herbicide launched May-2026.

FFB volume growth high single digit to early double digit for 4-5 years; area ~80,000 ha to ~1,50,000 ha (17,000 ha added in FY26); ~50% of plantations juvenile (0-4 years); Q1 margin dip from a state pricing-formula change; specialty-fats refinery from end-Aug/Sep-2026; downstream to add ~200 bp to overall EBITDA margin at scale; projects need 16-18% IRR.

60-70% of commodity inflation passed on; EBIT guidance ₹2,050-2,150 per tonne; cattle feed ~55-56% of volume, fish ~7%; poultry cut in chosen geographies; part of Q1 benefit from 'smart' buying 'may not be exactly structural'.
FY27 revenue growth 'at least more than 20%'; CDMO orders shifting to H2; CDMO ~50-52% of revenue; enterprise margins normalising as raw-material advantage fades.
Milk procurement prices high for 4 quarters and expected to stay for 2-3 more; ~70% passed on; war-led packaging inflation; 18-20 month route-to-market reset under a new CEO.
Live-bird trading to be cut 15-20% a year to near zero over ~5 years; B2C (Yummiez, RGC) 32% of the business, growing ~20%+; 3-4 years of investment phase; frozen chicken and momos launched.

guidance.value: Early double-digit revenue growth, mid-teens PBT growth (4-May-2026); 'double-digit' PBT growth (6-Aug-2026)
Close to ₹400 cr in FY27, then ₹300-350 cr a year from internal accruals; 75-80% growth capex; ~50% to oil palm

Invest: cattle feed, oil palm, crop care, branded foods. Reboot: Creamline, ACI, Astec. Reduce: RGC B2B, broiler feed. Strategic review: shrimp feed, seeds, cattle genetics. Close: live-bird trading. Some plants evaluated for closure.
Group evaluating the 'most optimal structure' for Astec and the chemicals business; update promised over 2-3 quarters (4-May-2026)

projects.project: Integrated palm oil complex (nursery, CPO mill; seed garden and refinery to follow in 18-24 months)

projects.status: Start end-Aug/early Sep-2026; ramp-up in H2FY27

management.note: Pay 180x median employee (FY26, part year); earlier career not covered in our sources

relatedParty.note: Pet-food back-end manufacturing for Godrej Pet Care (a Godrej Consumer company) earns ~₹9.5 cr a quarter, booked in other income (Q4FY26 call)

accounting: Animal Nutrition segment result now includes the cost of supplier financing (vendor invoice discounting); the company also shows an 'underlying' result excluding it (Q1FY27 ₹102 cr vs ₹84 cr reported).
Trade payables rose from ₹885 cr (Mar-25) to ₹1,651 cr (Mar-26) and Animal Nutrition segment liabilities from ₹648 cr to ₹1,379 cr: the working-capital gain is largely supplier credit.
Minority buyouts above book value were charged to equity (₹206 cr Godrej Foods FY25, ₹166 cr + ₹581 cr Creamline FY25-26), so reported equity fell while profit rose.
FY26 one-offs: land-sale gains ~₹34 cr (in EBITDA), wage-code charge ₹30.44 cr (exceptional), long-term incentive reversal in FY25 (₹15 cr).
Brands/goodwill of ~₹320 cr in gross block are not amortised; no impairment in FY26 (note 52).
